topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, introduces the lecture theme on the initiation and resolution of inflammation, and frames how the concepts connect to prior material.

topics.label: Principles of PAMPs, DAMPs, and Pattern Recognition Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular signatures of infection and damage and the general properties and subcellular localization of pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Toll-Like Receptors and Intracellular Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the diversity, cellular localization, and downstream transcriptional signaling pathways of Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Non-TLR Pattern Recognition Receptors and the Inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine additional pattern recognition receptor families and the multi-protein inflammasome complex responsible for processing pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cells respond to detection events and coordinate leukocyte recruitment from the bloodstream into infected tissue.

topics.label: Antigen Trafficking via the Lymphatic System
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells transport antigens through the lymphatic system to prime adaptive immune cells in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Pathology of Systemic Inflammation and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the life-threatening systemic consequences of excessive pro-inflammatory cytokine release during septic shock.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Inflammation Resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the passive decay and active biochemical regulatory mechanisms that terminate acute inflammatory signaling.

topics.label: Tissue Repair, Chronic Inflammation, and Granuloma Formation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological processes of tissue repair, the transition to chronic inflammation, and the formation of granulomas to contain persistent pathogens.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next session on the complement system.
